chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked him about a pen made of reeds that is placed in the water for fish, so the fish enter it and some of them die in it. He said: There is no harm with it.

Indeed, that pen was made only to catch fish in it. The way to reconcile these two narrations is to assume that if what died in the water is not distinguished from what did not die in it, and it is taken out, it is permissible to eat all of it.
But with distinction, it is not permissible in any case that indicates that.

key_terms.تَمْيِيز: Distinction or separation (of dead from live fish)
key_terms.حَظِيرَة: A pen or enclosure for catching fish
key_terms.قَصَب: Reeds, used to make the fish pen
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fish caught in a pen where some have died?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the permissibility of fish in a reed pen (hazirah) by distinguishing between cases where death is indistinguishable from life and those where it is not. It establishes that if dead fish cannot be identified, the entire catch is permissible, but if they can be distinguished, only the live ones are valid for consumption. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly approach to resolving apparent contradictions in hadith by applying contextual conditions to ensure purity and permissibility.
